name: Bolasterone (Finaject)

lead: Bolasterone is an oral methylated androgen originally made for veterinary use. People who write about it in steroid histories describe it as a mass and strength compound, with a low-to-moderate anabolic-to-androgenic ratio.

The chain is the usual androgen one: it activates the androgen receptor, which drives muscle protein gain, and more muscle and strength change how a physique looks. Most of what has been published about it concerns detection chemistry in doping control, and no human trials were found.

paras: In steroid histories it appears as an oral compound taken by mouth in cycles alongside training and diet, with muscle and strength gains discussed over weeks. It is rarely encountered today and is known mostly as a name in anti-doping literature.

No human safety data exist, so risks are inferred from other 17-alkylated oral steroids, which are associated with liver strain, hormone suppression and cholesterol changes. It is banned by WADA and controlled in some countries such as Brazil.

angle.text: Bolasterone is an oral methylated androgen aimed at more muscle and strength: it activates the androgen receptor, which speeds muscle protein gain and fills out the physique. Published work on it is mostly anti-doping detection chemistry, so its physique use rests on class effects.

lead: Bolasterone, chemically 7-alpha,17-alpha-dimethyltestosterone, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid developed by the Upjohn Company for veterinary use. Its 17-alpha-methyl group improves oral bioavailability and its 7-alpha-methyl group is shared with its isomer calusterone [1].

It is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency and is listed as a controlled anabolic steroid in Brazil [1]. Wikipedia notes an unreferenced claim that East German authorities obtained it for athletes through the state sports-medicine research institute [1].

Little published material covers bolasterone. Most of the scientific literature that mentions it concerns detection chemistry in doping control, not effects on people, and no clinical trials were found.

paras: Bolasterone is a testosterone derivative with methyl groups at positions 7 and 17. It is described as having a low-to-moderate ratio of anabolic to androgenic activity, comparable to fluoxymesterone [1].

No studies found. The published literature touching on bolasterone is analytical: for example, work on how 17-methyl steroids including bolasterone are epimerised and excreted in humans [2], and methods for detecting anabolic steroids in urine and horse samples [3].

Wikipedia lists the brand names Myagen and Methosarb and the developmental code U-19763 [1]. Because it is detected in anti-doping and horse-racing screens [3], it appears in the testing literature, but bolasterone has no established place in modern looksmaxxing or bodybuilding discussion. The compound is sometimes referenced in connection with veterinary use in racing animals, though that use is not documented in the sources reviewed here.
